ledger.hypothesis: this node is neither ELEMENTWISE nor QUERY -- it is O(1): three joints, one law-of-cosines solve. There is no collection to accelerate and nothing to thread (the whole pass is far under the 50 us region floor). The only real work is constant overhead: the generic nd:: engine allocated roughly forty shared_ptr<vector<double>> temporaries for 3-, 9- and 16-element vectors per solve, and the Maya side did ten findPlug(const char*) attribute-table walks per solve. Both are pure overhead that a hand lowering removes without touching a single arithmetic operation.

ledger.risk: bit-parity. The rewrite reproduces every operation in the source order: norm as sqrt of a left-to-right acc = acc + x*x fold; rot3 as (eye + s*k) + (1-c)*(k@k) with ascending-l accumulation from a zero accumulator; the full 4x4 w_rest @ delta including the delta[l][3] zero terms; the clamp spelled min-then-max exactly as lowered; the reach clamp keeping the source's (hi < mx ? hi : mx) direction and strictness. No comparison that selects a branch was narrowed or loosened, and -ffp-contract=off keeps the multiply-adds unfused, so the doubles follow the same rounding path the array engine took.

ledger.hypothesis: The node is neither ELEMENTWISE nor QUERY -- it is a fixed-size 3-joint analytic IK, O(1) in every benchmark knob. --bench-array 20000 and --bench-geo 400 do not reach it at all: an MPxIkSolverNode has no typed or array inputs, so the harness falls through to bench_ik_rig(), which builds a 4-joint chain plus an ikHandle and times cmds.getAttr('<tip>.worldMatrix[0]'). With no N to attack, the only levers are constant-factor: the ~70 std::make_shared<std::vector<double>> allocations the nd:: temporaries cost (every 3-vector is a heap array), and the ~14 string-keyed findPlug calls per solve.
